title: An Elementary Proof of the Hambly-Lyons Uniqueness Theorem
summary: We give a self-contained proof, in the bounded variation setting, of the Hambly--Lyons uniqueness theorem, which states that (total) signature identifies the path up to tree-like equivalences. The argument is organized around two key geometric observations. First, tree-like paths have trivial signature because factorization over a loop in a tree $τ:[0,1]\to T$ is preserved under signature lifts, which follows from an elementary property of planar curves.
